lost-wallet-cafe-01-a1-a2.metadataRec: Both speakers now named aloud; set nameSpokenInAudio=true for maria and mr_james.
lost-wallet-cafe-01-a1-a2.notes: Names introduced via a natural self-introduction between strangers (a standard ESL pattern). Mr. James is café staff, which makes the title plausible.

turns.text: Oh no. My wallet is not in my bag.
Excuse me. Is this brown wallet yours?
Yes, it is! Thank you so much. I am Maria.
You are welcome, Maria. I am Mr. James. It was near the door.
Thank you, Mr. James. I am very lucky today.

lost-wallet-cafe-01-b1-b2.metadataRec: Set nameSpokenInAudio=true for maria and mr_james.
lost-wallet-cafe-01-b1-b2.notes: Maria gives her name; the helper introduces himself as staff, anchoring both the name and his café role.

turns.text: Excuse me, I just ordered coffee, but I cannot find my wallet anywhere.
I think this may be yours. It fell from your bag when you came in.
That is it! I was sure I had lost it outside in the rain. I'm Maria — thank you.
You're welcome, Maria. I'm James, I work here. I picked it up before anyone stepped on it.
Thank you, Mr. James. You saved me a lot of trouble.

lost-wallet-cafe-01-c1.metadataRec: Set nameSpokenInAudio=true for maria and mr_james.
lost-wallet-cafe-01-c1.notes: Names woven into the exchange; he identifies as the café manager, keeping the C1 register intact.

turns.text: I have checked every pocket twice, and my wallet has somehow disappeared.
Before you panic, take a look at this. I noticed it sliding out of your bag as you stepped away from the entrance.
That is mine. I honestly thought it had fallen outside, and with this rain I would never have found it. I'm Maria, by the way.
Nice to meet you, Maria. I'm James — I manage the café. Luckily it landed just inside the door, so I picked it up before the next customer walked in.
I really appreciate your honesty, Mr. James. You turned a stressful moment into a small reminder that strangers can be kind.

shared-umbrella-bus-stop-01-a1-a2.metadataRec: All speakers are adults; retain nameSpokenInAudio=true for each dialogue speaker.
shared-umbrella-bus-stop-01-a1-a2.notes: Adult-character rewrite approved in July 2026; audio remains pending.

turns.text: It is raining hard, and I left my umbrella at home.
Come under mine. I am Ms. Clark.
Thank you, Ms. Clark. I am Leo. I do not want my work papers to get wet.
You are welcome, Leo. The bus is almost here.
Great. You saved my morning.

shared-umbrella-bus-stop-01-b1-b2.metadataRec: All speakers are adults; retain nameSpokenInAudio=true for each dialogue speaker.
shared-umbrella-bus-stop-01-b1-b2.notes: Adult-character rewrite approved in July 2026; audio remains pending.

turns.text: I checked the forecast before leaving for work, but it said the rain would start later.
That happens all the time. Come closer, or your laptop bag will get completely wet. I am Ms. Clark, by the way.
Thanks, Ms. Clark. I am Leo. My laptop and work papers are in there.
No problem, Leo. The bus is turning the corner, so we only need to wait another minute.
I appreciate it. Next time I will keep an umbrella in my office bag.

shared-umbrella-bus-stop-01-c1.metadataRec: All speakers are adults; retain nameSpokenInAudio=true for each dialogue speaker.
shared-umbrella-bus-stop-01-c1.notes: Adult-character rewrite approved in July 2026; audio remains pending.

turns.text: I should have known better than to trust a clear morning forecast. Now my laptop bag is taking the worst of the storm.
Step in a little closer. There is enough room, and it would be a shame to let your work equipment get soaked. I am Ms. Clark.
Thank you, Ms. Clark. I am Leo. I did not want to impose, but I was running out of dry places to stand.
It is no imposition, Leo. The daily commute is easier when people look out for one another.
That is true. A small courtesy can make a miserable journey feel almost pleasant.

torn-grocery-bag-01-a1-a2.metadataRec: Reclassify to roles: 'Dad' -> name 'the father' / role parent; 'Clerk' -> name 'the store clerk' / role store_staff. Set identityStrategy=role_only. The tutor must reference these by role, never by a proper name.
torn-grocery-bag-01-a1-a2.notes: Dad and Clerk are role labels, not proper names. The clerk states that he works at the store, and the parent role is clear from context.

turns.text: Oh no. The bag broke.
I work here. I can help you pick up the apples.
Thank you. The bread is on the ground too.
Here is a stronger bag from the store.
That is much better. Thanks for your help.

torn-grocery-bag-01-b1-b2.metadataRec: Reclassify to roles (father / store clerk); identityStrategy=role_only.
torn-grocery-bag-01-b1-b2.notes: Dad and Clerk are role labels, not proper names. The clerk states that he works at the store, and the parent role is clear from context.

turns.text: Careful, Mia. The bottom of the bag just tore, and the apples are rolling everywhere.
Do not worry, I work here. I will grab them before they go into the street.
Thanks. I should have used two bags because these groceries are heavier than I thought.
Here, put everything in this reusable store bag. It is stronger and easier to carry.
Perfect. Now my daughter and I can get home without losing dinner on the sidewalk.

torn-grocery-bag-01-c1.metadataRec: Reclassify to roles (father / store clerk); identityStrategy=role_only.
torn-grocery-bag-01-c1.notes: Dad and Clerk are role labels, not proper names. The clerk states that he works at the store, and the parent role is clear from context.

turns.text: Well, that was dramatic. One second we had groceries, and the next second dinner was escaping across the sidewalk.
I saw the bag give way from the register. Let me help before the apples roll any farther.
I appreciate it. My daughter is trying to rescue the bread, but I think the bag has officially retired.
This reusable one from the store should survive the trip home. It has wider handles and holds more weight.
Excellent. Next time I will not underestimate a harmless-looking bag full of apples.

shared-lunch-classroom-01-a1-a2.metadataRec: All speakers are adults; retain nameSpokenInAudio=true for each dialogue speaker.
shared-lunch-classroom-01-a1-a2.notes: Adult-character rewrite approved in July 2026; audio remains pending.

turns.text: Mina, I left my lunch at home before class.
You can have half of my sandwich, Sam.
Really? Thank you, Mina.
Of course. I also brought some fruit.
That is very kind. I will bring coffee tomorrow.

shared-lunch-classroom-01-b1-b2.metadataRec: All speakers are adults; retain nameSpokenInAudio=true for each dialogue speaker.
shared-lunch-classroom-01-b1-b2.notes: Adult-character rewrite approved in July 2026; audio remains pending.

turns.text: I came straight from work, Mina, and left my lunch on the kitchen table.
That is okay, Sam. I packed more than I need, so we can share during the break.
Are you sure? We still have another two hours of class this afternoon.
I am sure. You can have half the sandwich, and we can split the fruit.
Thanks, Mina. I will bring coffee for both of us next time.

shared-lunch-classroom-01-c1.metadataRec: All speakers are adults; retain nameSpokenInAudio=true for each dialogue speaker.
shared-lunch-classroom-01-c1.notes: Adult-character rewrite approved in July 2026; audio remains pending.

turns.text: I managed to bring every course handout, Mina, but somehow left my lunch sitting on the counter.
That sounds like the result of rushing here after work, Sam. Take half of my sandwich.
I appreciate it, Mina, but I do not want your generosity to become your afternoon hunger.
Do not worry. I packed more than enough, and our instructor will not mind if we finish the fruit during the break.
Fair point. I will provide the coffee next week as both a thank-you and emergency insurance.

pancake-practice-kitchen-01-a1-a2.metadataRec: All speakers are adults; retain nameSpokenInAudio=true for each dialogue speaker.
pancake-practice-kitchen-01-a1-a2.notes: Adult-character rewrite approved in July 2026; audio remains pending.

turns.text: Grandma Rosa, I promised to make pancakes for my friends, but this one is too dark.
That is okay, Leo. Turn down the heat.
I will use less batter this time.
Good. Wait for small bubbles before you turn it.
This one looks much better. Brunch may be saved.

pancake-practice-kitchen-01-b1-b2.metadataRec: All speakers are adults; retain nameSpokenInAudio=true for each dialogue speaker.
pancake-practice-kitchen-01-b1-b2.notes: Adult-character rewrite approved in July 2026; audio remains pending.

turns.text: I invited my friends for brunch, Grandma Rosa, but the first pancake burned.
That is how everyone learns, Leo. Lower the heat and watch for bubbles on top.
So I should wait until the edges look dry before I flip it?
Exactly. Then slide the spatula underneath and turn it over quickly.
This one is golden. I think my guests will actually get breakfast.

pancake-practice-kitchen-01-c1.metadataRec: All speakers are adults; retain nameSpokenInAudio=true for each dialogue speaker.
pancake-practice-kitchen-01-c1.notes: Adult-character rewrite approved in July 2026; audio remains pending.

turns.text: I volunteered to host brunch, Grandma Rosa, and my first pancake looks like evidence from a kitchen disaster.
It looks like practice, Leo. Pancakes are good teachers because they reveal every mistake immediately.
So the heat was too high, and I waited too long before turning it.
Right. Keep the pan medium-hot, use less batter, and flip when bubbles appear and the edges begin to set.
This one is actually golden. Perhaps my friends will trust me with brunch after all.

late-meeting-workplace-01-a1-a2.metadataRec: Set nameSpokenInAudio=true for Diego and Noah.
late-meeting-workplace-01-a1-a2.notes: The coworkers address each other by name; Diego matches the late worker shown in the image.

turns.text: I am sorry I am late, Noah.
It is okay, Diego. The meeting just started.
Did I miss anything important?
Not yet. We are looking at the plan.
Thanks. I will sit down quietly.

late-meeting-workplace-01-b1-b2.metadataRec: Set nameSpokenInAudio=true for Diego and Noah.
late-meeting-workplace-01-b1-b2.notes: The coworkers address each other by name; Diego matches the late worker shown in the image.

turns.text: Sorry I am late, Noah. The elevator stopped on almost every floor.
Do not worry, Diego. We have only reviewed the schedule so far.
Good. I was afraid I had missed the decision about the client presentation.
That part is next. I saved you a seat and opened the notes on my laptop.
Thanks, Noah. I will catch up quickly and add my comments after the overview.

late-meeting-workplace-01-c1.metadataRec: Set nameSpokenInAudio=true for Diego and Noah.
late-meeting-workplace-01-c1.notes: The coworkers address each other by name; Diego matches the late worker shown in the image.

turns.text: I apologize for slipping in late, Noah. The elevator queue downstairs was worse than I expected.
You are fine, Diego. We have covered the timeline, but the main discussion has not started yet.
That is a relief. I was worried I had missed the part where we divide the presentation tasks.
Not yet. I put the shared notes in front of you, and I marked the section where your input will matter most.
Perfect. I will listen for a minute, then jump in once I understand where the group has landed.

printer-help-workplace-01-a1-a2.metadataRec: Set nameSpokenInAudio=true for maya and liam.
printer-help-workplace-01-a1-a2.notes: Coworkers named by direct address in the first two turns.

turns.text: Liam, the printer is not working.
Let me look, Maya. Is there paper inside?
Yes, but the light is red.
The paper is stuck. I can fix it.
Great. I need these pages for the meeting.

printer-help-workplace-01-b1-b2.metadataRec: Set nameSpokenInAudio=true for maya and liam.
printer-help-workplace-01-b1-b2.notes: Names added by direct address without altering the troubleshooting steps.

turns.text: Liam, the printer stopped halfway through my report, and now it keeps flashing a red light.
That usually means a paper jam, Maya. Open this tray and pull the page out slowly.
I see it. The corner is folded, so it must have gone in at an angle.
Exactly. Once we remove it, press this button and send the file again.
Thanks, Liam. I still have time to bring the copies to the meeting.

printer-help-workplace-01-c1.metadataRec: Set nameSpokenInAudio=true for maya and liam.
printer-help-workplace-01-c1.notes: Both names woven into the first two C1 lines.

turns.text: Of course the printer waits until ten minutes before the meeting to become mysterious, Liam.
It is not being mysterious, Maya, just dramatic. The red light usually means a page is trapped inside the tray.
I can see the edge, but if I pull too hard I will tear it and make things worse.
Good instinct. Hold both sides and ease it out slowly. Then we will reset the tray before you print the report again.
Thank you, Liam. If this works, the meeting will never know how close it came to being paperless.

team-deadline-workplace-01-a1-a2.metadataRec: Set nameSpokenInAudio=true for sofia and omar.
team-deadline-workplace-01-a1-a2.notes: Teammates name each other in the opening turns.

turns.text: We have a lot of work today, Omar.
Yes, Sofia, but we can finish together.
I will check the pictures.
I will write the last notes.
Good. Then we can send the project.

team-deadline-workplace-01-b1-b2.metadataRec: Set nameSpokenInAudio=true for sofia and omar.
team-deadline-workplace-01-b1-b2.notes: Names added by direct address without changing the task split.

turns.text: The deadline is in one hour, Omar, so we need to choose what matters most.
I can finish the summary, Sofia, while you check the images and numbers.
That works. After that, we should read the whole project once more.
Agreed. If we find small mistakes, we can fix them before sending it.
I was nervous before, but now the plan feels possible.

team-deadline-workplace-01-c1.metadataRec: Set nameSpokenInAudio=true for sofia and omar.
team-deadline-workplace-01-c1.notes: Both names woven into the first two C1 lines.

turns.text: We are not going to polish every detail before the deadline, Omar, so we need to be strategic.
Agreed, Sofia. I will tighten the conclusion and remove anything that repeats information from the chart.
Good. I will verify the numbers and make sure the visuals support the main argument instead of distracting from it.
Once those pieces are done, we can read the project aloud. That usually reveals awkward sentences faster than staring at the screen.
Exactly. The deadline still feels close, but at least the work now has a shape we can finish.

office-break-room-01-a1-a2.metadataRec: Set nameSpokenInAudio=true for anna and marco.
office-break-room-01-a1-a2.notes: Original named only Marco (turn 1). Added Marco's direct address of Anna in turn 2 so both names are audible.

turns.text: Hi Marco. Are you on a break?
Yes, Anna. I need some water.
I have coffee and a snack.
Nice. The morning was busy.
Yes, but five quiet minutes help.

office-break-room-01-b1-b2.metadataRec: Set nameSpokenInAudio=true for anna and marco.
office-break-room-01-b1-b2.notes: Names added by direct address in the first two turns.

turns.text: You look relieved to be away from your desk, Marco.
I am, Anna. The morning was full of calls, and I needed a short break before the next one.
Same here. I made coffee, but I am mostly enjoying the quiet.
Sometimes five minutes in the break room makes the rest of the day easier.
Exactly. After this, I can go back with a clearer head.

office-break-room-01-c1.metadataRec: Set nameSpokenInAudio=true for anna and marco.
office-break-room-01-c1.notes: Both names woven into the first two C1 lines.

turns.text: You have the expression of someone who has survived a very long morning, Marco.
That is accurate, Anna. Three calls, two urgent messages, and one spreadsheet that refused to make sense.
Then this is a well-earned pause. I came in for coffee, but honestly I needed a few minutes without notifications.
There is something useful about stepping away before frustration starts making decisions for you.
Exactly. A short break does not solve the work, but it makes us better company for the work when we return.
